s: In die Herzen der Kameraden wehen Heimweh und Fernweh, und die Männer seufzen, seufzen in wohliger Sehnsucht.
Heimweh.et: Heim + Weh. Originally a medical term in Switzerland. Cognate to Alemannic German Häiwee, Bavarian Haimweh (Upper Austrian), Low German Heimweih.

s: Das Heimchen am Herde von Charles Dickens
The Cricket on the Hearth by Charles Dickens
Vielschichtiger gestaltet sind hier übrigens die Frauenrollen, egal ob Heimchen oder Kriegerin. Aber das ist ja auch Norwegen und nicht Deutschland.
Women's roles, be they hausfrau or warrior, have more layers of complexity here. But this is of course Norway and not Germany.
Heimchen.et: Heim + -chen. In the figurative sense popularized by the German title of Charles Dickens' The Cricket on the Hearth (1845), Das Heimchen am Herde.

s: home, one’s dwelling, the place where one is at home
a home, asylum, hostel (residence for some specified group)
a home, asylum, hostel (residence for some specified group): without further context usually short for either Kinderheim (“children’s home, orphanage”) or Altersheim (“retirement home”)
Mein Sohn / Vater ist im Heim.
My son / father lives in a home.
a home, asylum, hostel (residence for some specified group): a house, center for a collective purpose other than to dwell in
Heim.et: From Middle High German heim, from Old High German heim, from Proto-West Germanic *haim. Cognate with Dutch heem, English home, Danish hjem.

s: home, to the house; always as a direction, thus never in the sense of at home
Am Abend komm' ich dann auch gerne wieder heim.
In the evening, I like to get back home again.
heim.et: From Heim (“home”). Compare Middle High German heime (“home, at home”, adverb), from Old High German heime, heimi (“home, at home”, adverb).

s: home, home town, homeland, native land
Ich habe meine Heimat Türkei vor zwei Jahren verlassen.
I left my native Turkey two years ago.
Ländlich bodenständige Kinder waren die drei und wurzelten mit allen Herzensfasern in dem Stückchen Erde, das sie Heimat nannten.
The three of them were rural down-home children and were rooted with all fibres of the heart in the little piece of soil that they called home.
home; homeland; place where something originated or where it is deep-rooted
Bayern ist die Heimat von Brezeln und Weißbier.
Bavaria is the homeland of pretzels and wheat beer.
Heimat.et: First attested in the 11th century. From Middle High German heimuote, heimüete, from Old High German heimōti, heimuoti, from Proto-West Germanic *haimōdī (“homeland”). Compare Bavarian Hoamat, Silesian East Central German Heemte.

s: secret, clandestine (done or kept in secret)
heimlich.et: From Middle High German heimlich, heimelich, from Old High German heimilīh, from Proto-West Germanic *haimalīk. Equivalent to Heim + -lich.

Heimlichkeit.et: Middle High German heimlīchkeit, by surface analysis, heimlich + -keit.

s: an earlier form of Umweltschutz ("protection of the environment")
An animal from an animal shelter

A formal term for a pet, as opposed to a farm animal or a wild animal. In 1986 this definition of the term became a law in article 1 of the European Convention for the Protection of Pet Animals, German: Europäisches Übereinkommen zum Schutz von Heimtieren
Heimtier.et:
From Heim ("home") + Tier ("animal").
See also Tierheim

Heimtextilien.et: Plurale tantum, from the words Heim + Textilien.

s: domestic (internal to a specific nation or region)
Das Mpox verursachende Virus ist in West- und Zentralafrika heimisch und gehört der gleichen Virusfamilie an wie jenes, das früher die Pocken auslöste.
homely (characteristic of or belonging to the home; domestic)
[…] Dem Mann aus Schleswig-Holstein stellte sie eine Tasse mit der Aufschrift »Moin« auf den Schreibtisch. »Damit du dich in diesem wunderbaren Amt gleich so richtig heimisch fühlst«, sagte Baerbock.
heimisch.et: From Middle High German heimisch, from Old High German heimisk; by surface analysis, Heim + -isch.
